desc:
The string words holds one or more non-empty words separated by single commas, for example "flower,flow,flight".

Return the length of the longest string that is a prefix of every word. If the words share no first letter, return 0.

words = "flower,flow,flight"   -> 2   ("fl")
words = "dog,racecar,car"     -> 0
words = "alone"               -> 5   (a single word is its own prefix)
constraints: Each word has at least one letter
Words consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Take the first word as a candidate prefix and compare it with the other words, one position at a time.
You can scan column by column: at position i, every word must have a letter there and it must equal the first word's letter at i. Stop at the first column that fails.
A shortcut: the common prefix of all words is the common prefix of the alphabetically smallest and the alphabetically largest word, because every other word sorts between them.
editorial: Vertical scanning is the classic approach. Let first be the first word. For column i = 0, 1, ... check that every other word is long enough and has the same letter as first[i]. The first column where this fails (or where some word ends) is the answer. The work is at most the total number of letters, so O(total length).

A neat alternative: in sorted order, all words lie between the smallest and the largest word, so any prefix shared by those two is shared by all words in between. Finding the min and max costs one pass, and comparing the two costs at most the shortest length. Horizontal scanning (shrinking a running prefix word after word) works equally well.
solution:
def commonPrefixLength(words):
    ws = words.split(",")
    lo, hi = min(ws), max(ws)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lo) and i < len(hi) and lo[i] == hi[i]:
        i += 1
    return i
